title: Etale locality on source-and-target for scheme morphism properties
statement: Let $P$ be a property of morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], where etale morphisms mean [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The property $P$ is etale local on source-and-target if all three conditions hold: (i) for schemes $X,Y,Z$ and maps $a:X\to Y$, $f:Y\to Z$, if $a$ is etale and $P(f)$ then $P(fa)$; (ii) for schemes $X,Y,V$ and maps $f:X\to Y$, $b:V\to Y$, if $P(f)$ and $b$ is etale then the base change $X\times_Y V\to V$ has $P$; (iii) for every scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, $P(f)$ holds if and only if for every point $x\in X$ there are schemes $U,V$, etale maps $a:U\to X$ and $b:V\to Y$, a map $h:U\to V$ and a point $u\in U$ such that $a(u)=x$, $fa=bh$, and $P(h)$. No isomorphism-invariance, Noetherian, separation, quasi-compactness, or surjectivity assumption is part of this definition.
